decisive_items: Revealed herniation into the greater sciatic foramen with proximal ureteral dilatation
Shows proximal ureter dilation and hydronephrosis
presented with intermittent pain in right lumbar and abdomen
response.rationale: CT directly shows herniation into the greater sciatic foramen causing proximal ureteral dilatation and hydronephrosis, matching the obstructive symptoms. R9 identifies the hernia but omits the ureteral obstruction consequence; R11 only notes hydronephrosis without etiology.

rejected.why: Pain alone is nonspecific; anti-inflammatory relief and imaging favor obstruction, not stones.
Neoplasm lacks supporting imaging or history; herniation is the demonstrated cause.
Chronic inflammation is a symptom pattern, not the specific imaging-based diagnosis.
Identifies hernia but misses the ureteral obstruction and hydronephrosis as the key complication.
Overly broad inflammatory label; imaging specifies herniation.
Fever/chills are nonspecific; imaging is decisive.
Hydronephrosis is a finding, not the underlying diagnosis.
No renal parenchymal changes or pyelonephritis-specific imaging; herniation is the cause.
Stricture is contradicted by herniation as the cause of dilatation.
Retroperitoneal fibrosis not supported; herniation is explicit.
